newsitem.title: JAPAN: Isuzu says in engine sale talks with GM.
newsitem.headline: Isuzu says in engine sale talks with GM.

text.p: Isuzu Motors Ltd said on Friday that it had developed fuel-efficient 2,500 cc and 3,000 cc diesel engines and that it was negotiating to sell the engines to General Motors Corp.
Isuzu is 37.4 percent owned by GM.
The new engines, to be unveiled at a car show in Switzerland in early March, are aimed mainly at the European market, Isuzu said.
"We are negotiating with GM as well as other car makers over their possible purchase of the new engines," an Isuzu spokesman said.
He said Isuzu expected GM to buy its new engines, but he added that nothing had yet been decided.
Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shinbun said on Friday that Isuzu would provide the engines to the GM group as early as 1999. Isuzu is also negotiating with Honda Motor Co Ltd, the paper said.
